name: MediQore Clinical Rules Table
notice: Version 0 for the prototype on synthetic data only (LI-10). Every value is a WHO-referenced default that the Clinical Advisor has not yet reviewed. Do not use with real patients until the table is signed (M4 FE-4, LI-12).

references.who_pcpnc_2015: WHO. Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition. Geneva: WHO; 2015.
references.who_mcpc_2017: WHO. Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth: a guide for midwives and doctors, 2nd edition. Geneva: WHO; 2017.
references.who_anc_2016: WHO. WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience. Geneva: WHO; 2016.
references.who_hb_2011: WHO. Haemoglobin concentrations for the diagnosis of anaemia and assessment of severity (WHO/NMH/NHD/MNM/11.1). Geneva: WHO; 2011.
references.who_hb_2024: WHO. Guideline on haemoglobin cutoffs to define anaemia in individuals and populations. Geneva: WHO; 2024.
references.who_tetanus_2017: WHO. Tetanus vaccines: WHO position paper, February 2017. Weekly Epidemiological Record 2017;92(6):53-76.
references.who_stillbirth_2016: WHO. Making every baby count: audit and review of stillbirths and neonatal deaths. Geneva: WHO; 2016 (stillbirth at 28 or more completed weeks for international comparison).
references.nhsrc_nip_2022: Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination (NHSRC). National Immunization Policy 2022. Islamabad: Government of Pakistan; 2022.
references.who_unicef_sam_2009: WHO and UNICEF. WHO child growth standards and the identification of severe acute malnutrition in infants and children: a joint statement. Geneva: WHO; 2009.
references.who_sam_2013: WHO. Guideline: updates on the management of severe acute malnutrition in infants and children. Geneva: WHO; 2013.
references.who_growth_2006: WHO Multicentre Growth Reference Study Group. WHO Child Growth Standards: length/height-for-age, weight-for-age, weight-for-length, weight-for-height and body mass index-for-age. Geneva: WHO; 2006.
references.who_imci_2014: WHO. Integrated Management of Childhood Illness: chart booklet. Geneva: WHO; 2014.
references.roadmap: MediQore Full-Stack Implementation Roadmap, 10 Oct 2026 (Module 3: range checks to catch typing errors).

visit_entry_checks.description: Typing-error checks on the visit form (M3 FE-1). A value outside 'allowed' cannot be saved and the server refuses it. A value inside 'allowed' but outside 'plausible' is saved only after the LHW confirms it.
visit_entry_checks.review_note: Only systolic BP 60-250 comes from the roadmap; the other ranges are proposals for the Clinical Advisor.

pulse_counter.description: When the BP device shows no pulse, the LHW taps once per beat for this many seconds and the app multiplies the count (M3 FE-1).

blood_sugar_conversion.description: A reading typed in mg/dL is stored in mmol/L: mmol/L = mg/dL / factor.

maternal_risk.description: Danger-sign rules checked on the phone after every visit, independently of the model (M4 FE-4). The final level is always the higher of the model result and the rule result.

rules.description: Systolic BP 160 mmHg or above, or diastolic BP 110 mmHg or above.
BP 140/90 mmHg or above together with severe headache, blurred vision or severe/upper abdominal pain.
Fever and too weak to get out of bed.
Temperature 38 °C or above together with another danger sign.
Absent or markedly reduced fetal movement. The form's 'reduced' option means markedly reduced.
Severe anaemia signs (for example very pale palms or inner eyelids with breathlessness).
BP 140/90 mmHg or above on its own sets the level to at least Yellow, with a facility check.
rules.review_note: The scope leaves the time for the facility check to the approved protocol: the Clinical Advisor sets facility_check_within_hours.

flags.description: Swelling is recorded and shown as a flag; it does not change the risk level.

anaemia.description: Anaemia flag from a verified haemoglobin value with its date and source (M6 FE-2). The flag never changes the risk colour unless the signed table says so.
anaemia.review_note: WHO 2011 bands for pregnant women. The 2024 WHO guideline (who_hb_2024) uses 10.5 g/dL instead of 11.0 in the second trimester; the Clinical Advisor chooses which to apply.

obstetric_history_flags.description: Risk-factor flags from the obstetric history and age at registration (M2 FE-2). They are shown on the profile and result screens and never change the risk colour unless the signed table says so.

flags.description: A known medical condition was recorded.

obstetric_history_flags.review_note: The scope names 'Previous C-section' as an example. The other flags and their cut-offs are proposals for the Clinical Advisor.

pregnancy_outcomes.description: A pregnancy that ends at or after this gestational age without a live birth is a stillbirth; before it, a miscarriage (M6 FE-4).

anc_schedule.description: Antenatal contacts generated from the gestational age at registration (M6 FE-1). Contacts already past at registration are skipped.

tetanus_toxoid.description: TT/Td doses for a pregnant woman without earlier doses (M6 FE-1). The first dose is given at the first contact; each later dose has a minimum interval from the previous one.

supplements.description: Daily iron and folic acid throughout pregnancy; the app tracks compliance against this (M6 FE-1).

epi_schedule.description: Routine EPI schedule for children under 2 (M8 FE-1). For each dose: dose number, minimum age, recommended age, minimum interval from the previous dose of the same antigen, maximum age where applicable. A late child's next dose is due at the later of the recommended age and the previous dose date plus the minimum interval.
epi_schedule.review_note: Verify every row against the current Federal Directorate of Immunization schedule. Maximum ages (for example the rotavirus and OPV-0 limits) are left null where the schedule does not state them; the Clinical Advisor fills them in.

zero_dose_indicator.description: A child with no recorded Penta-1 after its recommended age (M8 FE-2).

nutrition.description: MUAC classification for children aged 6-59 months; bilateral pitting oedema means SAM regardless of MUAC (M9 FE-1). No wasting classification.

z_scores.description: Weight-for-age (underweight) and height-for-age (stunting, only when height is measured) from the WHO Child Growth Standards tables, bundled with the app in Phase 3.

imci.description: IMCI decision logic for a sick child aged 2 months up to 5 years (M9 FE-3). Severity colours follow the chart booklet: pink (urgent referral), yellow (treat), green (home care). The Urdu and English action texts live in the app's language files under each action key.
imci.review_note: The scope's checklist names respiratory rate, chest indrawing, stool frequency and dehydration signs. The IMCI logic also uses the general danger signs, listed here so the Phase 3 checklist can include them; the Clinical Advisor confirms the list.

cough_or_difficult_breathing.when: no signs of pneumonia or very severe disease
